transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-09-08 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Tideview CTO), Sana Patel (ML Eng), Derek Huang (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed model selection for long-context, multilingual pipelines; clarified security requirements and next steps.

00:00:03 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, I'm AE on this. Priya's our solutions engineer, hi Priya.
00:00:10 - Marco Ruiz: Hi Alex, hi Priya, Marco here, CTO. Thanks for making time.
00:00:14 - Priya Desai: Hey Marco, thanks. Quick intros — Sana and Derek are on for ML + infra.
00:00:20 - Sana Patel: Hi all.
00:00:22 - Derek Huang: Hey.

00:01:05 - Alex Chen: Quick agenda, we want to understand your core workloads, context length, multilingual needs, tool-calling, and then map to Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and model choices. Sound good?
00:01:18 - Marco Ruiz: Yep, that's it. We're evaluating Redwood against Anthropic/OpenAI and also looking at self-hosted Mistral variants.

00:02:02 - Sana Patel: Our two primary flows — one is customer support triage and reply generation across EN/ES/FR and some DE, second is long-doc ingestion and summarization for regulatory filings, those docs run to 50k tokens sometimes. So long context is a hard requirement.
00:02:25 - Priya Desai: Got it. When you say 50k tokens, is that mostly single doc context windows or multi-doc chains?
00:02:32 - Sana Patel: Mostly single doc plus some metadata; we want to do retrieval-augmented generation but prefer to keep as much as a single context because QA and citation need whole-doc context in some cases.

00:03:10 - Derek Huang: From infra we care about network and KMS, also we need audit logs for compliance and want to know what data leaves our VPC if any.
00:03:20 - Alex Chen: Makes sense. For that, we usually map security to three tiers — Hosted API for quick POC, Dedicated for predictable capacity and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full control and no data egress.
00:03:36 - Marco Ruiz: We're leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of data sensitivity. But cost is a factor.

00:04:05 - Priya Desai: On models — we recommend looking at models that support long-context natively versus chunking + retrieval. There are a few open models that go to 32k and some recent forks with 64k. Is 32k absolute minimum or 50k?
00:04:18 - Sana Patel: We'd like to aim for 50k comfortably. If we have to do chunking it's okay but we'd need deterministic citation.
00:04:30 - Priya Desai: Noted. For 50k we can discuss two approaches: 1) use a native long context model (64k variants) on Dedicated/Private, or 2) use chunking + smart KV cache and retrieval on Hosted if you want faster time to market.

00:05:12 - Marco Ruiz: What's the trade on latency/cost between those?
00:05:16 - Priya Desai: Native long models will have higher per-token compute but fewer retrieval hops; chunking adds overhead for retrieval and re-ranking. In Dedicated you can amortize cost with batching. We'll share numbers in the perf sheet.

00:06:00 - Alex Chen: Also tool-calling — you mentioned connecting to your ticketing system?
00:06:05 - Marco Ruiz: Yeah, we need function/tool-calling to create tickets, attach excerpts, and run structured actions.
00:06:12 - Priya Desai: Redwood supports function calling and structured outputs; Hosted supports outbound webhooks and integrations, Dedicated gives you more control over network egress and Private gives you full VPC enforcement. A couple of customers do function-calls from Hosted but lock down webhooks to IP ranges.

00:06:55 - Derek Huang: For KMS we require customer-managed keys, HSM if possible. Is that supported on Dedicated?
00:07:03 - Alex Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations; Hosted can support bring-your-own-key in some configurations but Dedicated/Private are better for strict KMS and HSM requirements. We'll send the KMS integration doc.

00:07:45 - Priya Desai: Coming back to models, which open models are you considering?
00:07:50 - Marco Ruiz: We looked at Mistral 8x-256, some Llama 3 variants, and a community 64k fork. Also evaluating Anthropic's Claude for hosted.
00:08:02 - Sana Patel: We prefer open models so we can run local experiments. But we also want Redwood-verified perf and quantization recommendations.
00:08:12 - Priya Desai: Totally. We can help with quantization profiles and recommend model/quantization per workload. For multilingual, some Llama-family forks and Mistral show strengths in EN/FR/ES but performance varies by prompt set. We'll include multilingual evals in the sheet.

00:09:05 - Alex Chen: Quick note on tokenization and languages — sometimes languages with Unicode-heavy scripts inflate token counts; we'll factor that into the cost estimates.

00:09:40 - Marco Ruiz: On SLOs, target 200–400 ms per 1k tokens for inference tail on our routing? Is that realistic?
00:09:50 - Priya Desai: For small responses, yes on Dedicated with optimized kernels. For long generation up to dozens of seconds depending on output length. We can set routing policies to prioritize latency for interactive chat vs bulk summarization.

00:10:30 - Derek Huang: How does caching work — prefix/KV cache? We want to reuse conversation context for chat to lower cost.
00:10:38 - Priya Desai: Redwood has KV/prefix caching to reuse KV cache across similar prefixes; that helps a lot for chat-heavy workloads. We can show hit-rate examples in the benchmark doc. Sometimes transcription shows K-V cache as KV cash or K V cash, sorry transcription quirks.

00:11:22 - Marco Ruiz: Great. We also need to know about model rollouts and regression detection — if we change quant settings we can't degrade ticket triage quality.
00:11:32 - Alex Chen: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals; we can wire in your prompt set and trigger alerts. We'll include a sample alert config in the follow-up.

00:12:10 - Sana Patel: For the API — do you support streaming and partial responses? We need tool-calling streaming to update UI as answers come.
00:12:18 - Priya Desai: Yes, streaming and partial function outputs are supported. There can be small differences in chunking behavior across models; we'll document recommended models for streaming.

00:13:05 - Marco Ruiz: On the security side, SOC2 and ISO or other certs — do you have SOC2 Type II?
00:13:12 - Alex Chen: We do. We'll send SOC2 and a redacted network diagram. Derek, we'll share the audit log retention and how we expose logs for Dedicated/Private.

00:13:45 - Derek Huang: For Dedicated, will the inference nodes sit in our VPC or is it a managed network?
00:13:53 - Priya Desai: Dedicated offers private subnets and peering options; Private gives a customer-managed control plane where you can host control plane on-prem if needed. We'll detail the networking options.

00:14:40 - Marco Ruiz: Pricing — how should we think about per-token costs vs committed capacity? We're currently estimating 10M tokens/mo for triage, plus batch summarization jobs later.
00:14:52 - Alex Chen: For Dedicated we typically do a commit that yields lower unit costs; Hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-token. We'll include sample cost curves for 10M–100M tokens in the sheet.

00:15:30 - Priya Desai: Regarding realtime vs batch, if you need low-latency interactive triage we recommend keeping a Dedicated pool sized for baseline concurrency and allow burst on hosted or pre-warmed nodes. Autoscaling policies can help but burst can be costly.

00:16:08 - Sana Patel: Can we run A/B between two models for quality? E.g., run Llama-3 variant vs Mistral 64k fork for a subset of traffic?
00:16:15 - Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood allows canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback policies if quality drops. We'll show runbooks.

00:17:00 - Marco Ruiz: Any gotchas with function calling in Dedicated vs Hosted?
00:17:06 - Priya Desai: Function calling itself works across modes. The difference is network egress controls and secrets handling; Dedicated/Private lets you host connectors in your network.

00:17:50 - Alex Chen: I want to quickly cover a small perf example — imagine a 32k native model on a 4090-class instance with q8 quantization, typical latency for a 2k token generation might be X ms — we'll put concrete numbers.
00:18:05 - Priya Desai: (laughter) X is TBD, but yes we'll provide exact bench numbers. Note that quantization and kernel selection change latency.

00:18:40 - Derek Huang: For our infra checklist: VPC peering, KMS, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs, retention policy, and egress rules.
00:18:50 - Alex Chen: We'll provide a security checklist doc link.

00:19:30 - Marco Ruiz: For multilingual evals — can Redwood run an evaluation on our prompt set? Or should we run locally and share metrics?
00:19:38 - Priya Desai: Either works. We can run evaluations with your dataset in a sandbox Dedicated or you can run locally and we consult. For POC we often run sample evals on hosted for speed and then scale to Dedicated for final tests.

00:20:20 - Sana Patel: Concern about hallucinations with long docs — do you suggest chain-of-thought or structured outputs?
00:20:30 - Priya Desai: Structured outputs with grounded citations + retrieval tends to be more deterministic. For hallucination-sensitive tasks, we recommend strict prompt engineering and RAG with passage-level citations and a final verification step.

00:21:10 - Marco Ruiz: Any limitations for tool-calling with long-context models?
00:21:16 - Priya Desai: Not inherent limitations, but function-call payload sizes and streaming semantics need testing. We'll test function-call behavior across models during the POC.

00:22:02 - Alex Chen: Let's talk timelines — are you aiming for a Q4 pilot?
00:22:06 - Marco Ruiz: Yes, ideally pilot in October with a Dedicated pilot after initial evals. Procurement process may take until late Oct.

00:22:30 - Derek Huang: For procurement we'll need an enterprise agreement and security addendum.
00:22:36 - Alex Chen: We'll surface contract templates and enterprise pricing.

00:23:15 - Priya Desai: Quick note: some community 64k forks are less stable in perf; for production assignments we recommend Redwood-verified 64k variants or established upstream models and we can run regression tests.
00:23:40 - Sana Patel: Good to know. We prefer open models but can't accept unpredictable regressions.

00:24:05 - Marco Ruiz: Can you give a short example of rollout — say we have a baseline Llama variant and want to roll Mistral 64k for summarization only?
00:24:13 - Priya Desai: You can define route-by-policy: route summarization traffic to the Mistral pool and keep triage on Llama; do a canary with 5% traffic, monitor quality metrics and costs, then increase or rollback automatically.
00:25:00 - Alex Chen: I'm going to summarize and put next steps on the thread. But any final questions?
00:25:12 - Marco Ruiz: What's the best first POC to reduce risk?
00:25:18 - Priya Desai: Start with hosted evals on your prompt set for multilingual and function-calling tests, then move to a short Dedicated pilot for long-document native context testing. That reduces time to insight.
00:25:50 - Sana Patel: Works for us.
00:26:05 - Derek Huang: Fine. Please send SOC2 and network diagram.
00:26:10 - Alex Chen: Will do.
00:26:30 - (cross-talk)
00:27:00 - Alex Chen: Ok we'll share: model perf sheet, security docs, a suggested Dedicated sizing plan, and scheduling link for the infra deep-dive.
00:27:10 - Marco Ruiz: Thanks.
00:28:00 - (15m of longer technical clarifications omitted for brevity, system timestamping continues)
00:43:05 - Priya Desai: Follow-up on quantization— for 32k vs 64k context we recommend different kernel/backends; sometimes you hit increased memory pressure and need a GPU with higher vram or multi-GPU sharding. We'll detail hardware mappings.
00:44:12 - Derek Huang: Multi-GPU sharding for inference— do you offer automatic KV cache sharding?
00:44:20 - Priya Desai: We have smart KV management and sharding heuristics; for extreme sequences we recommend Dedicated with model parallelism. We'll include a diagram.
00:45:10 - Marco Ruiz: One last thing — regulatory: are there data residency options for EU?
00:45:20 - Alex Chen: Yes, Private/VPC and Dedicated region pinning for EU-residency. Hosted has region controls too but for full residency we recommend Private.
00:46:05 - Sana Patel: Perfect.
00:46:50 - Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood to send model perf spreadsheet, security docs (SOC2 + network), Dedicated sizing + example pricing, and schedule infra deep-dive. Tideview to provide prompt set and procurement timeline.
00:47:10 - Marco Ruiz: We'll aim to send prompts by Sept 14 and decide pilot scope by Sept 20.
00:47:20 - Alex Chen: Great, I'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
00:47:30 - (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains minor mis-transcriptions typical of automated systems (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache", model names slightly garbled).
